title: Sulfur-doped g-C3N4/g-C3N4 isotype step-scheme heterojunction for photocatalytic H2 evolution

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Pristine g-C3N4 evolves little H2 under visible light; efficient metal-free photocatalysts are needed. S-doping g-C3N4 to pair S-doped and S-free domains as an isotype S-scheme heterojunction should raise H2 evolution.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/modification), n5 (PRC/synthesis), n6 (PRC/treatment), n7 (PRC/treatment), n8 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Sulfur is bonded into the heptazine framework as C-S-C (S on N sites) in S-g-C3N4-E. S-g-C3N4-E is highly porous: SBET 173.53 m2/g and Vpore 0.888 cm3/g, >10x g-C3N4-E and S@g-C3N4-E.
states.detail: Absorbed: n9 (STR/chemistry/bonding), n10 (STR/microstructure/porosity), n11 (STR/interface). Premises: S 2p near 164.5 eV marks C-S-C bonding; 168.5 eV marks oxidised sulfur (SO4 2-); Sulfur melts near 115 C and boils near 445 C, so it is liquid at 180 C and vapour at 520 C; S-scheme model: contact of oxidation- and reduction-type semiconductors aligns Fermi levels, bends bands and sets an internal field that recombines the useless carriers

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Internal field recombines O-domain CB electrons with R-domain VB holes, leaving R-domain electrons (-0.64 V) to reduce H+ and O-domain holes (2.25 V) to oxidise TEOA. Photogenerated charges separate more efficiently and recombine less in S-g-C3N4-E than in g-C3N4 and g-C3N4-E.
states.detail: Absorbed: n12 (MEC/pathway), n13 (PRP/value), n14 (PRP/value). Premises: S-scheme model: contact of oxidation- and reduction-type semiconductors aligns Fermi levels, bends bands and sets an internal field that recombines the useless carriers; Higher photocurrent, quenched PL and longer PL lifetime indicate better photogenerated charge separation

states.title: Performance state
states.head: S-g-C3N4-E keeps evolving H2 over six 4-h visible-light cycles (24 h)

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: S-doping plus pyrolysis turns exfoliated g-C3N4 into a porous S-doped/S-free isotype S-scheme photocatalyst with ~49x higher H2 evolution

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: H2 accumulates linearly to ~22,400 umol/g in 4 h on S-g-C3N4-E; the other three samples stay near zero. H2 evolution rate of S-g-C3N4-E under >420 nm light is 5548.1 umol/g/h
nodes.solves: S-g-C3N4-E gives by far the highest H2 evolution rate of the four samples, 5548.1 umol/g/h at >420 nm
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: 22,400/4 h ~ 5600 umol/g/h, consistent with the 5548.1 bar in F6d

nodes.title: PL, F7, F8
nodes.head: Photocurrent ranks S-g-C3N4-E (~0.3-0.55 uA) > g-C3N4-E (~0.13-0.2) > g-C3N4 (~0.07-0.1) > S@g-C3N4-E (~0.05). PL band near 460 nm is far weaker for S-g-C3N4-E than for g-C3N4 and g-C3N4-E.
nodes.solves: Photogenerated charges separate more efficiently and recombine less in S-g-C3N4-E than in g-C3N4 and g-C3N4-E
nodes.op: compare across conditions, correlate across series, fit model
nodes.note: S-g-C3N4-E shows sharp spike-and-decay transients and its peak current falls from ~0.55 to ~0.41 uA over six cycles extra ~435 nm peak in S@g-C3N4-E and a shoulder in S-g-C3N4-E PL quench does not track activity across the four samples, so quenching alone does not show better separation; photocurrent and H2 yield of S@g-C3N4-E from F7b and F6a (o22, o15)
nodes.detail: o22: Photocurrent ranks S-g-C3N4-E (~0.3-0.55 uA) > g-C3N4-E (~0.13-0.2) > g-C3N4 (~0.07-0.1) > S@g-C3N4-E (~0.05); o24: PL band near 460 nm is far weaker for S-g-C3N4-E than for g-C3N4 and g-C3N4-E; o25: S@g-C3N4-E PL is also strongly quenched (peak ~45% of g-C3N4), although it has the lowest photocurrent and near-zero H2 yield; o26: PL decay curves of all four samples nearly overlap; S-g-C3N4-E decays only marginally slower; o28: Two-exponential lifetimes of S-g-C3N4-E exceed g-C3N4's by only 1-5% (6.826 vs 6.735 ns; 1.749 vs 1.667 ns)
